chapter: Hines 1935-38, Gus Arnheim and Billy Eckstine
title: Writing for Billy Eckstine with Earl Hines
summary: Budd writes Eckstine's vocal charts, including 'I Love the Rhythm in a Riff' and 'Water Boy', while Hines pays little per chart.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah, great comedian and everything. So, when Earl -- when Earl hired Billy Eckstein, he didn't have any music, you know. So, I started to write a few things for him. He -- he got a little disgusted. He said, "Man, I'm going to get out of the band. I ain't got nothing to sing." To Earl. I said, "Let me write something for the man."

Well, see, Earl was thinking about the money. He wasn't paying me but ten, 15 dollars for an arrangement, you know. And, so, I started to write some things for Billy Eckstein to sing. And, I practically wrote all of his music for him to sing.
What were some of those first things for him?
Well, "I Love the Rhythm in the Riff".

One of What are the things he wrote. What the hell was the name of it? Oh, and we did pop music, you know, I was writing -- 'cause those publishers used to come around and song pluggers with their pop tunes, and I would write them. They would come so fast, I really can't remember them all.
I would -- but later on I can tell you some of the stuff that I did for him after -- after he left Earl's band.

But, anyway -- but, I remember that I love The Rhythm in the riff because I really liked that arrangement... And, Billy used to sit down and he would hum it to me and I would write -- oh, "Water Boy".
We did that in the bus while we were riding to a gig one time.
That was a great hit for him, then.
Yeah, "Water Boy". Oh, you don't know what love is. "Sky Lark".
Then -- and these things, you know, I wrote. They're sort of coming back to me now.
